restated: Let f(q,r) be the unique p such that (p,q,r) is a P-position of 3-row Chomp, defined by the Brouwer recurrence; for each fixed r let N(r) be the least q0 >= r such that the sequence f(q,r)-q is periodic for all q >= q0 (if row r has only finitely many P-positions, i.e. f(q,r) < q for all large q, N(r) is instead the least q with f(q,r) < q). Define B_c(a)=f(c+a,c)-(c+a) (undefined where no loser [c,a,b] exists), u_c=N(c)-c, p_c=the period of f(q,c)-q for q >= N(c) (p_c:=1 for rows with finitely many P-positions), q_r=lcm{p_c : 0<=c<r}, m_r=1+max{B_c(a) : 0<=c<r, a>=0}, U_r=max{u_c:c<r}, t_r=max(U_r,r). Then for every r>=1: (i) m_r<=r+1; (ii) p_r<=q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r); (iii) u_r<=max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r); (iv) q_{r+1}<=q_r^2(r+2)^(r+1). Hence N(r)<=r+max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r) for rows with infinitely many P-positions, and N(r)<=r+1+max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r) otherwise. Every quantity on the right is computed from the rows c<r alone, so this is an effective recursion for N(r).
ledger_statement: CORRECTED ZEILBERGER RECURSION (repairs C0013). In Zeilberger coordinates [c,a,b] with B_c(a)=f(c+a,c)-(c+a), u_c=N(c)-c, p_c=period(c) (p_c:=1 for stale rows), q_r=lcm{p_c:c<r}, m_r=1+max{B_c(a):c<r,a>=0}, U_r=max{u_c:c<r}, t_r=max(U_r,r): for every r>=1, (i) m_r<=r+1 (C0012, cited prior art); (ii) p_r<=q_r(m_r+1)^{m_r}; (iii) u_r<=max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^{m_r}; (iv) q_{r+1}<=q_r^2(r+2)^{r+1}. Hence N(r)<=r+max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^{m_r} for live rows (stale rows similar with +1). This is an EFFECTIVE recursion for N(r): every right-hand quantity is computed from the already-solved rows c<r. The instant-winner preperiod bound t_r (Lemma P in the proof) is the piece C0023 flagged as missing; the false closed form of C0013 is NOT restored.

verdicts.gap_description: As literally stated (i) is false: at r=1, a=0 one has B_1(0)=f(1,1)-1=2 > 1=r (the only violation in r<=400 and sampled rows to r=5000); what C0012 gives is B_r(a) <= r+1, which is what the proof body actually derives and all that (iv) and the state bound require. A second fillable gap: the load-bearing sentence "Zeilberger's Lemma Bounded then applies with M = m_r: every defined B_r(a) <= m_r" is cited but never stated or proved (it is true: if v=max L_a > m_r then v-1 forces L_{a-1}=v, inductively L_0=v, but L_0=mex(W_r(0)) <= m_r), and the stale-row facts (contiguous definedness, terminator B_r(a*)=0) are asserted without proof; all were verified numerically and are short arguments.

verdicts.effectivity_check: Effective, not a reassertion of existence: the constants are produced. Quote: "(iii) u_r <= max(t_r, m_r) + q_r (m_r + 1)^{m_r}" and "(iv) q_{r+1} <= q_r^2 (r + 2)^{r + 1}", together with "m_r <= r + 1" and the explicit base q_1 = p_0 = 1 (row 0 has constant B_0 = 1). Substituting the bounds recursively gives a pure recursion in r alone (q_{r+1} <= q_r^2 (r+2)^{r+1}, u_r <= max(t_r, r+1) + q_r (r+2)^{r+1}), so N(r) is bounded by a finite integer computable from r with a program or calculator; no step appeals to a quantity known only to exist. Caveat honestly admitted by the submission: this is a recursion, not a closed form — a closed form needs (Z2), a bound on lcm{period(c): c<r}, which remains open — and the resulting bound is enormous (log q_r grows like 2^r), though fully computable.
